  "instruction_summary": "Fix all violations of three security properties in /app/docvault.py (a Python HTTP service on port 8080). (1) No header injection: strip all CR and LF from user-supplied data before it goes into any response header value. (2) No open redirect: if a user-supplied redirect target starts with http://, https://, or //, set Location to / instead; relative paths work normally. (3) No cookie attribute injection: strip all semicolons from user-supplied data before it goes into any Set-Cookie header value. User-supplied data includes JSON body fields, query parameters, URL path segments, and data stored in the database that originally came from users. All existing endpoints and behavior must continue working. The reported symptom: POST /api/docs with author containing \\r\\n creates extra response headers.",
  "solution_outline": [
    "Add three helper functions to docvault.py: strip_crlf(value) removing \\r and \\n, sanitize_redirect(url) returning '/' for URLs starting with http://, https://, or //, and strip_semicolons(value) removing ';'",
    "Fix Site A: wrap author in strip_crlf() before passing to X-Authored-By header in POST /api/docs",

    "Fix Site D: apply sanitize_redirect() and strip_crlf() to row['url'] in GET /api/go/{code} before setting Location header",

    "Fix Site F: wrap urllib.parse.unquote(title_encoded) result in strip_semicolons() before using in Set-Cookie in POST /api/docs/{title}/star"
